text: The rule Lesson 30 built fires for real, three weeks later, against the same accounts-payable account from Lesson 29's Alert C - impossible travel, then a mailbox rule change, aimed at Thornfield Financial Services. This time it runs the full lifecycle: detection, triage, escalation, investigation, resolution, and the metrics it leaves behind.

Two ordinary sign-in records, one from Windows Event Forwarding and one from the mail platform's own audit log, are Chapter 3's log collection at work - neither says attack on its own. Chapter 4's correlation rule is what turns them into one alert, grouping the login pair by user, calculating an impossible travel speed, and raising severity the instant the mailbox rule change lands seconds later. Chapter 5's triage process is what gets it escalated: every criterion met at once.

Tier 2 goes further than a shift's worth of triage allows. The mail audit trail shows three forwarded invoices, all from real vendors, caught before any payment moved. A sweep of other accounts finds no sign the same technique hit anyone else. The conclusion: a confirmed business email compromise aimed at redirecting a vendor payment, not a random credential test.

Resolution disables the account, revokes its sessions, deletes the malicious mailbox rule, and blocks the external address at the mail gateway, with new credentials, re-enrolled MFA, and the legacy protocol that skipped MFA disabled for good. Chapter 6's dashboard metrics capture the result: fast detection because the correlation rule fired on both signals at once, a fuller resolution time that's expected for a case this serious, and one contained line in next week's leadership report.

Once the analyst confirms the compromise, Chapter 7's SOAR playbook runs the repeatable containment steps automatically - disable, revoke, delete the rule, post the summary - cutting roughly 40 minutes of manual work down to under 3. The analyst still makes every judgment call; the playbook only acts once that call is made.
One incident, five chapters working together in the order the SOC actually uses them. Next up: tying every chapter in this course together one last time.
